title: Memory Prices Set to Rise Again in Q4 as Samsung and SK Hynix Race to Expand Capacity
source_used: BigGo Finance (fulltext from main session); an aggregator drawing on TrendForce, DRAMeXchange, Gartner and Korean media
key_facts: TrendForce projected on 30 Sep 2026 that Q4 contract prices for commodity DRAM will rise 10% to 15% from the prior quarter and NAND flash 15% to 20%.
DRAMeXchange: average fixed price for PC DRAM (DDR4 8Gb) was $26 in September, up 4.0% on August and about 16 times April of last year; TrendForce raised its Q4 PC DRAM forecast from 3-8% to 13-18%.
TSMC has reportedly decided to raise production prices by 5% to 10% from early 2027.
Samsung's preliminary Q3 operating profit was 107.4 trillion won (about $80.5 billion), the first quarter above 100 trillion won.
Gartner estimates 2027 memory revenue at $1.0755 trillion, up 28.4%, with memory exceeding non-memory chip revenue for the first time.

SK Group chairman Chey Tae-won said on 11 Oct 2026 in Shanghai: 'We need to expand quickly.' He moved the Yongin cluster's completion target from 2045 to 2033; Samsung is considering bringing forward its Pyeongtaek P5 and Yongin schedules.
Views differ on whether new supply will lower prices: CXMT's volume ramp could amplify declines once the crunch eases, but Yuanta Securities expects tight supply through 2027-2028.
Micron's Taoyuan union held a strike authorization vote on 7 Oct (about 99% in favour); timing and form of any strike are undecided.
quote_evidence: Market research firm TrendForce projected on the 30th of last month that Q4 contract prices for commodity DRAM will rise 10–15% from the prior quarter.
NAND flash is expected to climb 15–20%.
On the other hand, the prevailing view on the Street is that tight supply-demand conditions will persist into next year.
why_it_matters_hint: Memory costs feed into the price of phones, PCs and AI servers; the figures are research-firm forecasts and analysts disagree on how long the shortage lasts.
event_date: TrendForce forecast 30 Sep 2026; Chey remarks 11 Oct 2026; article 12 Oct 2026
notes: Read in full. This is a BigGo roundup of earlier events; several strands were carried in our editions of 8 to 10 Oct 2026 (Samsung's record profit estimate, Micron's Taoyuan union, Samsung's long-term supply deals). BigGo names TrendForce and DRAMeXchange but not its Korean press sources.
